title: Hunk
character: Man at beach with drink (uncredited extra)
verdict_short: No. He's a blink-and-miss beach extra.
how: Pitt is a background extra in a single beach scene of this Faustian body-swap comedy. His nameless character has no dialogue and no arc, so nothing happens to him. Widely considered his first on-screen film appearance.
notes: Uncredited. Included for completeness; not a credited role.

title: No Way Out
verdict_short: No. Just a face in the party crowd.
how: Pitt appears as an uncredited party guest in this Kevin Costner political thriller.
notes: Uncredited extra work.

title: No Man's Land
verdict_short: No. He serves a table and exits.
how: Pitt plays a waiter in a restaurant scene.
notes: Uncredited.

title: Less Than Zero
verdict_short: No. Background partygoer, unharmed.
how: Pitt is a background extra at a party.
notes: Uncredited extra.

title: Another World
verdict_short: No. A high-school basketball kid in two soap episodes.
how: Pitt's first speaking TV role: Chris, a teenage basketball player, in the May 14 and 15, 1987 episodes of the NBC soap. The part is a bit role with no dramatic jeopardy; he simply appears and is gone.
notes: Two episodes only.

title: Growing Pains
verdict_short: No. Sitcom heartthrob, twice over, never in danger.
how: In "Who's Zoomin' Who?" (November 1987) Pitt is Jeff, the cute transfer student Carol's friends push her toward. In "Feet of Clay" (February 1989) he plays Jonathan Keith, Ben's rock-star idol who turns out to be a jerk backstage. Both are family-sitcom guest spots; nobody dies.
notes: Two different characters across two seasons.

title: Dallas
verdict_short: No. Charlie Wade's boyfriend gets banned, then un-banned.
how: Across four episodes (December 1987 to February 1988, season 11) Pitt plays Randy, the boyfriend of Charlie Wade. Ray Krebbs forbids Charlie from seeing him for a while, then relents when her behavior improves. Randy simply drifts out of the storyline alive.
notes: Four episodes.

title: Trial and Error
verdict_short: No. He carries bags in a sitcom and leaves.
how: Pitt's first paid Hollywood job, shot in November 1987, three days after arriving from Missouri. He plays a hotel bellboy in the second episode of this short-lived CBS sitcom. Zero jeopardy.
notes: Aired March 22, 1988; the series was cancelled after three episodes.

title: 21 Jump Street
verdict_short: No. He's the friend who yells at Penhall, not the kid who dies.
how: In this May 1988 episode, a troubled teen the Jump Street cops are investigating takes his own life, sending Penhall into a spiral. Pitt plays Peter, the boyfriend of a girl in the friend group, who confronts Penhall over his odd behavior. The death is another character; Peter walks away fine.
notes: Some sources list the character as Jeff Deiner; IMDb credits him as Peter.

title: A Stoning in Fulham County
verdict_short: No. He changes his plea to guilty and gets a suspended sentence.
how: Teddy is one of the teens who hurl rocks at an Amish buggy from a pickup, killing a seven-month-old baby. The prosecutor struggles to get the pacifist Amish family to testify. In the courtroom climax Teddy switches his plea to guilty as the Amish family walks in; the epilogue says the boys were fined and given suspended sentences.
notes: NBC TV movie based on a real 1979 Indiana incident.

title: The Dark Side of the Sun
verdict_short: Yes. He takes off the mask, feels the sun, and lets the disease win.
how: Rick has a rare skin disease that makes any light lethal, so he lives in a full leather suit and mask. After a Yugoslav healer fails and the actress he loves rejects his unmasked face, Rick decides to stop hiding: he strips off the protection and feels sunlight on his skin for the first time. The disease then takes its course, and his father accepts the choice he made.
notes: Pitt's first lead. Shot in 1988 in Yugoslavia, unreleased until 1997. The death is implied rather than shown as a drawn-out scene.

title: Head of the Class
verdict_short: No. Dim hunk survives a sitcom episode.
how: In the January 1989 episode "Partners", Pitt is Chuck, a handsome but not-so-bright guy that gifted student Maria dumbs herself down to impress. Pure sitcom fluff; nobody is in danger.
notes: Often mislisted as Bobby; IMDb credits the role as Chuck.

title: Freddy's Nightmares
verdict_short: No. Freddy leaves him alive but trapped in adulthood.
how: Newlyweds Rick and Miranda break down in Springwood. Rick's half of the episode is a nightmare gauntlet: he's hit by a hit-and-run driver, robbed by an elderly couple, dreams of piranhas at a motel, and learns he was the hit-and-run driver from the opening. Miranda ends up childlike after a head injury, so Rick is left alive but shackled to responsibility.
notes: Anthology episode "Black Tickets". The nightmares are dream logic, not literal deaths.

title: thirtysomething
verdict_short: No. The babysitter's boyfriend, alive and glowing.
how: Pitt plays Bernard, the boyfriend of the Steadmans' babysitter, in a brief love scene in the season three episode "Love and Sex". Producers said he caused a stir on set. Nothing bad happens to him.

title: Cutting Class
verdict_short: No. Framed for the murders, he survives the drill-in-a-vice finale.
how: Dwight is the bad-boy boyfriend everyone suspects when bodies pile up at school, thanks to a ring with his initials planted at a crime scene. The real killer is asylum-returnee Brian Woods. In the shop-class climax Brian clamps Dwight's head in a vice and goes at him with a drill; Paula brains Brian with a claw hammer and he falls onto a running saw. Dwight and Paula drive off together.
notes: Dark-comedy slasher; Brian (Donovan Leitch) is the one who dies.

title: Happy Together
verdict_short: No. Minor college pal in a rom-com.
how: Pitt's Brian is a small supporting part in this mismatched-roommates college romance starring Patrick Dempsey and Helen Slater. The plot is about the roommates falling in love and finishing their degrees; Brian is peripheral and unharmed.

title: The Image
verdict_short: No. Junior newsroom staffer, untouched.
how: In this HBO drama about TV anchor Jason Cromwell (Albert Finney), whose bank-scandal report drives a wrongly accused executive to take his own life, Pitt plays Steve Black, a young reporter on the news team. He's a minor presence and the death is another character's.
notes: HBO TV movie, premiered January 1990.

title: Too Young to Die?
verdict_short: No. The sleazy hustler lives; the girl he corrupted gets the gas chamber.
how: Billy is the drug-dealing hustler who exploits 15-year-old runaway Amanda (Juliette Lewis), pushing her into drugs and strip clubs. After she's dumped by soldier Mike Medwicki, Billy drugs her and goads her into revenge: they kidnap Mike and his girlfriend and Amanda stabs Mike to death with Billy's knife in an oilfield. Both are arrested; the film follows Amanda being tried as an adult and sentenced to death. Billy survives.
notes: Fact-based NBC TV movie.

title: Glory Days
verdict_short: No. Cancelled after six episodes, alive.
how: Pitt is Walker Lovejoy, one of four high-school friends drifting apart in this Fox drama. Walker is a college dropout turned cub reporter. The show was cancelled after six episodes with no death for the character.
notes: Fox series, six episodes.

title: Across the Tracks
verdict_short: No. Runs the big race and keeps breathing.
how: Straight-A track star Joe is chasing a Stanford scholarship when his delinquent brother Billy (Rick Schroder) comes home from juvie and joins a rival school's team. The brothers' rivalry culminates in a head-to-head race with Joe's future on the line. It's a drama about brothers learning a lesson; nobody dies.

title: Thelma & Louise
verdict_short: No. Steals the cash and walks; the women drive off the cliff.
how: Drifter J.D. charms Thelma into a motel-room night and then robs the women of Louise's $6,700 life savings, which triggers Thelma's turn to armed robbery. He's later picked up and questioned by the police, who use him to help track the women. J.D. is alive and in custody when Thelma and Louise fly the T-bird into the canyon.
notes: Pitt's breakout role.

title: Johnny Suede
verdict_short: No. Learns life is more than a pair of suede shoes.
how: Pompadoured wannabe rock star Johnny gets magic black suede shoes, chases bohemian Darlette (and dodges her gun-toting boyfriend), pawns his guitar, and loses her. He forms a band with Deke and ends up with the smarter Yvonne, who teaches him there are more important things than shoes. Comic drift, no death.
notes: Pitt's first true starring vehicle in the U.S.

title: Contact
verdict_short: No. Buries a dead Iraqi soldier and parts ways with the other.
how: Lost in the Iraqi desert during the Gulf War, American soldier Cox picks his way through a minefield and comes face-to-face with Iraqi soldier Mohannan (Elias Koteas). He can't pull the trigger after seeing Mohannan look at a family photo. A poison-gas warning forces them to cooperate; the film ends with the two burying a dead Iraqi and going their separate ways.
notes: 30-minute short, Oscar-nominated for Best Live Action Short.

title: Cool World
verdict_short: Yes. Holli shoves him off a Vegas hotel roof. Then he's reborn as a cartoon.
how: Detective Frank Harris, a WWII vet stuck in the animated Cool World since 1945, tries to stop Holli Would from escaping into the real world. In the climax atop the Union Plaza Hotel, Holli pushes him off the building to his death. But a 'noid' killed by a 'doodle' in the real world is reborn as a doodle, so Frank returns to Cool World as a cartoon and can finally be with Lonette.
notes: Dies as a human, resurrected as an animated character. Counts as a death with a happy loophole.

title: A River Runs Through It
verdict_short: Yes. Beaten to death over gambling debts, off-screen.
how: Charismatic, self-destructive Paul is a brilliant fly fisherman and newspaperman drowning in drink and poker debts. After a last golden day fishing with his father and brother, the police inform Norman that Paul was beaten to death; his body was found in an alley with the bones of his casting hand broken. The circumstances are left deliberately mysterious.
notes: Death reported, never shown. Based on Norman Maclean's real brother.

title: Tales from the Crypt
verdict_short: Yes. Loses the drag race to the Iceman and goes up in a fireball.
how: Cocky psycho drag racer Billy rolls into town to goad Sheriff Joe Garrett, secretly the legendary racer 'Iceman', into one last race. When Joe refuses, Billy seduces and then kidnaps his daughter Carey to force him behind the wheel. In the midnight race Billy slams into a digger parked in the road and dies in a fireball while Joe wins.
notes: Season 4 episode "King of the Road", directed by Tom Holland. Also released as a segment of the compilation TV film Two-Fisted Tales (1992).

title: Kalifornia
verdict_short: Yes. Shot dead by the writer he terrorized.
how: Kentucky parolee Early Grayce joins writer Brian and photographer Carrie on a cross-country serial-killer road trip and turns out to be a killer himself, murdering strangers and finally shooting his own girlfriend Adele. At an abandoned nuclear test site he kidnaps Carrie. Carrie clubs him with a mannequin limb, and when he keeps coming Brian shoots him dead.

title: True Romance
verdict_short: No. Never leaves the couch or the honey-bear bong.
how: Floyd is Dick Ritchie's perma-stoned roommate who spends the whole movie on the sofa. He cheerfully gives the Mafia hitmen the location of the drug deal and later does the same for the cops, but nobody bothers to hurt him. The Beverly Ambassador shootout happens without him.
notes: Scene-stealing cameo.

title: The Favor
verdict_short: No. Ends up planning a wedding.
how: Elliott is Emily's young artist boyfriend in this rom-com about Kathy asking her best friend to sleep with her old flame. Emily gets pregnant, Kathy meddles about the paternity, but once it's clear the baby is Elliott's he steps up. The film ends with Kathy helping Emily plan her wedding to Elliott.
notes: Shot in 1991, shelved until 1994.

title: Interview with the Vampire
verdict_short: No. He's been undead since 1791 and still is.
how: Louis, turned by Lestat in 1791, is the immortal narrator telling his story to a journalist in 1990s San Francisco. He survives Lestat's attempted murders, the Théâtre des Vampires burning, and centuries of misery. The film ends with a revived Lestat attacking the interviewer in his car, but Louis himself is very much still around.
notes: Technically 'dead' as a vampire, but the character never perishes. Claudia, not Louis, is destroyed by sunlight.

title: Legends of the Fall
verdict_short: Yes. Killed fighting a grizzly bear as an old man in 1963.
how: After a life of war, grief, bootlegging and revenge, Tristan outlives nearly everyone he loves. The epilogue, narrated by One Stab, jumps to 1963: an aged Tristan investigating an animal carcass in the North Country is confronted by a grizzly. He draws his knife and fights it, and dies in the struggle, a 'good death' that bookends the bear that clawed him at age twelve.
notes: Shown briefly on screen and narrated. Samuel, Isabel Two and Susannah all die before him.

title: Seven
verdict_short: No. He lives, but what's in the box destroys him anyway.
how: Rookie detective Mills hunts the seven-deadly-sins killer John Doe alongside Somerset. In the desert finale a delivery box arrives containing the head of Mills' pregnant wife Tracy; Doe confesses he is 'envy' and that Mills must become 'wrath'. Mills shoots Doe dead, completing the killer's design, and is led away alive but broken.
notes: Tracy (Gwyneth Paltrow) dies off-screen; Mills survives.

title: 12 Monkeys
verdict_short: No. The twitchy red herring survives; the plague isn't even his.
how: Jeffrey Goines is the mental-patient son of a virologist who founds the Army of the Twelve Monkeys. Cole assumes he's behind the apocalyptic virus, but Jeffrey's big crime turns out to be releasing zoo animals. Cole is the one shot dead at the airport; Jeffrey is last seen alive and unhinged.
notes: Oscar-nominated supporting turn.

title: Sleepers
verdict_short: No. Throws the case, quits, and becomes a carpenter in England.
how: Michael, one of four Hell's Kitchen boys abused at a juvenile home, grows up to be an assistant DA who deliberately sabotages his own prosecution of his friends for killing guard Nokes, exposing the other abusers. The epilogue says Michael quits the DA's office, moves to the English countryside and becomes a carpenter. His friends John and Tommy die young; Michael doesn't.

title: The Devil's Own
verdict_short: Yes. Shot in a final boat standoff with the cop who took him in.
how: IRA gunman Frankie McGuire hides as 'Rory Devaney' with NYPD sergeant Tom O'Meara's family while buying Stinger missiles. Once exposed, he boards a boat to sail the weapons home. Tom follows; in the shootout Tom is wounded and disarmed, and Frankie is about to finish him when he realizes he too has been shot. He dies in Tom's arms as Tom steers the boat back to shore.

title: Seven Years in Tibet
verdict_short: No. Goes home to Austria and takes his son climbing.
how: Austrian mountaineer Harrer is interned by the British in India, escapes to Tibet, and becomes tutor and friend to the young Dalai Lama. When China invades in 1950 he leaves Tibet and returns to Austria, where he reconciles with the son who once rejected him. The film closes with the two climbing together.
notes: The real Harrer lived until 2006.

title: Meet Joe Black
character: Joe Black / the young man in the coffee shop
verdict_short: Yes and no. The coffee-shop guy is flattened by two cars; Death borrows his body, then gives it back alive.
how: Early on, the charming young man Susan meets in a coffee shop steps into the street and is fatally struck by multiple cars in one of cinema's most replayed deaths. Death then wears his body as 'Joe Black' to shadow Bill Parrish. At the end Joe walks Bill over the bridge into the afterlife, and the original young man returns, alive and unaware of where he's been, to rekindle things with Susan.
notes: The body dies at the start and is restored at the end; Death itself obviously can't die. Pitt plays both.

title: Saturday Night Live
verdict_short: No. Plays David Spade's shrink in the cold open.
how: In the November 7, 1998 cold open, David Spade visits his therapist, played by Pitt, to complain about the burdens of fame. It's a one-sketch cameo with no peril.
notes: Season 24. Sketch appearance, not a hosting gig.

title: Being John Malkovich
verdict_short: No. On screen for about half a second, mid-frown.
how: In the mock documentary about Malkovich's puppeteering career, Pitt appears as himself for a split second, looking miffed and about to speak before the cut. No fate, no lines.
notes: Uncredited cameo.

title: Fight Club
verdict_short: Sort of. The Narrator shoots himself through the cheek and Tyler blinks out of existence. But Tyler was never real.
how: Tyler Durden is revealed to be the Narrator's dissociated alter ego. With Project Mayhem's bombs about to level the credit-card towers, the Narrator realizes the gun in Tyler's hand is really in his own and fires it through his cheek. Tyler, gushing blood from the back of his head, collapses and vanishes. The Narrator survives, and he and Marla watch the buildings fall.
notes: Tyler is a hallucination; his 'death' is the Narrator's psyche reasserting control. The body Pitt plays never physically existed.

title: Snatch
verdict_short: No. Fakes taking a dive, wins the fight, and his camp settles up with Brick Top.
how: Bare-knuckle champion Mickey is ordered by gangster Brick Top to throw a fight; when Mickey refuses, Brick Top has his mother burned alive in her caravan. Mickey pretends to comply, then knocks his opponent out in the fourth round while his people ambush and kill Brick Top and his men outside. The travellers vanish before dawn.
notes: Mickey's mum dies; Mickey doesn't.

title: The Mexican
verdict_short: No. Delivers the cursed pistol, keeps the girl, drives into the sunset.
how: Bungling errand boy Jerry is sent to Mexico to retrieve the legendary 'Mexican' pistol while his girlfriend Sam is held by hitman Leroy. Bodies drop around him, including Leroy and mob boss Margolese's rival, but Jerry survives every mishap, returns the gun to Margolese, and ends the film on the road with Sam.

title: Spy Game
verdict_short: No. Muir buys him out of a Chinese prison with Operation Dinner Out.
how: Bishop is caught by the Chinese trying to spring his lover Elizabeth Hadley from prison and is scheduled for execution within 24 hours. Retiring mentor Nathan Muir spends his last day at Langley, and his own savings, faking authorization for a Navy SEAL rescue. Bishop and Hadley are lifted out by helicopter, and Bishop realizes Muir saved him when the pilot names the op.

title: Friends
verdict_short: No. Storms out of Thanksgiving still hating Rachel Green.
how: Ross's formerly-fat high-school friend Will comes to Monica's Thanksgiving and reveals he and Ross co-founded the 'I Hate Rachel Green Club' and spread a nasty rumor about her. The episode ends with Will, Ross and Rachel bickering and everyone alive.
notes: Pitt and Jennifer Aniston were married at the time. Emmy-nominated guest turn.

title: Ocean's Eleven
verdict_short: No. Eats his way through a $160M heist and drives off with Danny.
how: Rusty is Danny Ocean's right hand in the Bellagio vault job. The crew pulls off the heist, Benedict is fooled, and Rusty is last seen picking Danny up outside prison with Tess in tow. Perpetually snacking, never in danger.
